title: Ironclad VPC Guard Terraform module for egress, SGs, NACLs, and private DNS
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a reusable, auditable Terraform module (Ironclad VPC Guard) to standardize perimeter security for Private/VPC deployments. The module will encapsulate secure defaults and easy overrides for security groups (SGs), network ACLs (NACLs), private DNS forwarding/zone bindings, and egress control policies. It should support: scoped least-privilege SG rules, tag-based SG generation for workload teams, explicit NACL templates for public/private subnets, conditional private DNS forwarding (resolver endpoints / conditional-forwarders), and a declarative egress allowlist with optional proxy or NAT targets. The module must be testable with terraform-integration tests and include an upgrade path and health-check outputs for automation and console observability.
design_notes: Primary goals: enforce least-privilege egress, provide deterministic defaults for new clusters, and give platform teams simple opt-in controls for exceptions.
Expose a small surface area: `allowed_egress_destinations`, `workload_tags` (for auto-SG), `nacl_profiles` (predefined presets), and `private_dns_routes` (zone -> resolver mappings).
Prefer tag-based automation over explicit IP lists where possible; provide optional IPSet integration for exceptions tied to vendor IP ranges.
Module will emit monitoring metrics (via aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarms or datapoints to agents) for rule hits, denied-egress-count, and DNS-forward-fallbacks to surface misconfigurations.
Upgrade strategy: follow semantic module releases, include a migration guide for NACL changes (breaking for ephemeral subnets), and a `plan-only` CI job to detect destructive diffs before apply.
Security policy: include a Sentinel/OPA policy example that prevents allow-all egress rules in production workspaces.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module implements security_groups with parametrized least-privilege rules and supports tag-driven generation.
Module supports at least two NACL profiles (strict, permissive) and can apply to subnet lists without manual rule duplication.
Private DNS: module can create VPC resolver associations and conditional-forwarding rules for customer on-prem resolvers and supports split-horizon zones.
Egress: declarative allowlist is enforced; attempts to create infra with unrestricted 0.0.0.0/0 outbound are rejected by example Sentinel policy.
Health checks: module exports a `module_guard_status` output with reasons for blocked rules and a small TF test harness validates expected deny/allow behavior.
Automated terraform-integration pipeline includes `plan-only` safety gating and a `non-destructive-upgrade` job for minor release bumps.
Documentation + migration guide published in Confluence and linked in the module README with examples for Dedicated and Private installs.
tasks: T1: Define module schema and variable list; implement examples for three common workloads (api, batch, db)
T2: Implement SG generation engine with tag selector and template overrides
T3: Implement NACL profile templates and idempotent application across subnets
T4: Add private DNS resolver association and conditional-forwarder resources
T5: Implement declarative egress allowlist and proxy/NAT hooks
T6: Add CloudWatch metrics and module outputs for health checks
T7: Write terraform-integration tests (terragrunt/terraform testing harness) and pipeline jobs
T8: Draft upgrade and migration docs and sentinel policy examples
T9: Review + security assessment and shepherd through security review
testing_plan: Unit-level static checks with tflint and checkov; integration tests run in ephemeral AWS accounts to validate SG/NACL interactions and DNS forwarding using small test VPC. CI includes `plan-only` gating that posts diffs to the PR. Additional chaos test: simulate DNS resolver failure and assert route fallback/exported health metric increments.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Deploy module to one non-prod infra workspace for platform team services
Stage 2 (wider staging): Apply to staging clusters and run automated traffic tests to validate egress behavior
Stage 3 (production opt-in): Allow individual teams to opt-in by switching to `ironclad_vpc_guard` module and run `plan-only` job for 48 hours
Stage 4 (enforce): After 2 weeks of stable canaries, flip enforcement Sentinel policy in production workspaces
